items.text: The system shall provide visible entry points into the careers experience from both general Six Flags pages and park-specific pages.
items.annotation_notes: The sequence shows a general site, a jobs-focused page, and a White Water park page with hiring content, indicating multiple user-facing paths into job discovery.
items.manual_verification_notes: the entry point in the main web page is on the top menu under "Jobs" and not directly in the main page integrated

claims.claim: A general Six Flags page exposes a visible entry point into the careers or jobs area.
A park-specific page exposes recruiting or application entry points.

items.evidence_note: Step 1 shows a Jobs navigation item. Step 5 shows White Water recruiting content with Apply Now actions.
items.rationale: Visible entry points into careers are present on both the general Six Flags page and the park-specific recruiting page.

items.text: The system shall support choosing a specific park to scope job discovery to a particular location.
items.annotation_notes: Multiple screens show park selection as a central step, including a generic park chooser and a jobs page that becomes scoped to Six Flags White Water.

claims.claim: The jobs experience provides a visible mechanism for choosing a park.
The chosen park is reflected before continuing into park-scoped recruiting content.

items.evidence_note: The selector opens a park list and later shows Six Flags White Water, Atlanta, GA as selected.
items.rationale: The screenshots show both the park selection mechanism and the selected park state.

items.text: The system shall carry the selected park context into subsequent recruiting screens and park-specific job content.
items.annotation_notes: After park selection, later screens reference Six Flags White Water and then show a White Water Atlanta lifeguard posting, indicating location context persists across the flow.

claims.claim: The selected park context is shown before continuing.
Later recruiting and job-detail states preserve the selected park context.

items.evidence_note: White Water appears in the selected park field, the park recruiting page, and the Lifeguard job location.
items.rationale: The selected park context is visibly carried through later screens.

items.text: The system shall provide an individual detail page for a specific job opening.
items.annotation_notes: The final screen is a dedicated role page for a Lifeguard position, showing that openings can be represented as standalone job-detail views.

claims.claim: The flow reaches a standalone page for one specific job opening.
The page is dedicated to a Lifeguard opening rather than a generic job overview.

items.evidence_note: Step 6 is titled Lifeguard - up to $13/hour and contains job-specific details.
items.rationale: A specific individual job detail page is visible.

items.text: The system shall let applicants browse opportunities by department or specialized team within a selected park.
items.annotation_notes: The White Water page exposes team-oriented job areas such as lifeguards, food and beverage, park services, admissions, security, retail, and more opportunities.

claims.claim: The selected park recruiting page exposes department or team-based opportunity areas.
The visible opportunity areas include multiple teams rather than a single undifferentiated list.

items.evidence_note: Step 5 shows Food & Beverage, Lifeguards, Retail, Security, Admissions, Park Services, and More Opportunities cards.
items.rationale: The park recruiting page visibly supports browsing by team or department.

items.text: The system shall highlight featured or currently hiring roles on park recruiting pages to speed job discovery.
items.annotation_notes: The park page prominently promotes hiring content such as NOW HIRING LIFEGUARDS, category cards, and a mega hiring event, which suggests featured discovery support.

claims.claim: The park recruiting page prominently highlights currently hiring or featured role content.
The highlighted hiring content includes visible actions that support faster job discovery.

items.evidence_note: Step 5 includes a Now Hiring Lifeguards panel and multiple Apply Now actions.
items.rationale: Featured hiring content is visibly emphasized on the park recruiting page.

items.text: The system shall present core metadata for each opening, including role title, job category, requisition identifier, employment type, location, and posting information.
items.annotation_notes: The job detail page visibly includes structured opening information beyond the title, which supports a requirement around transparent job metadata.

claims.claim: The job detail page displays role title, job category, and requisition identifier.
The job detail page displays employment type, location, and posting information.

items.evidence_note: Step 6 shows Lifeguard - up to $13/hour, Job Category: In Park, a requisition number, Part-Time, White Water Atlanta location, and a posted date.
items.rationale: The visible job page presents the requested core metadata fields.

items.text: The system shall present role responsibilities, qualification criteria, and compensation information to support application decisions.

claims.claim: The job detail page presents role responsibilities and qualification criteria.
The job detail page presents compensation information.

items.evidence_note: Step 6 includes What You Will Be Doing, How You Will Do It, What You Will Need, and payrate information.
items.rationale: The job page visibly provides application decision-support information.

items.text: The system shall provide a prominent action for starting an application from recruiting content and job-opening pages.
items.annotation_notes: Apply Now calls to action are visible on the park recruiting page and again on the detailed opening page, supporting application initiation from multiple points.

claims.claim: The park recruiting page provides prominent application-start actions.
The specific job-opening page provides a prominent Apply now action.

items.evidence_note: Apply Now actions are visible on the park recruiting page and the Lifeguard job detail page.
items.rationale: The flow provides clear application-start actions from both recruiting content and the job page.

items.text: The system shall support an application workflow that can be launched for a specific opening after the applicant has identified the relevant park and role.

claims.claim: The applicant identifies a relevant park and reaches a specific role page.
The downstream application workflow or application form is reached after launch.

items.evidence_note: The flow shows park selection, role discovery, and an Apply now action, but not a launched application workflow.
items.rationale: The visible setup for launching an application is present, but the captured flow stops before a confirmed application-start page or form.

items.text: The system shall communicate employment perks, benefits, or similar value propositions alongside job discovery content.
items.annotation_notes: Several screens include perks and benefits messaging or benefit bullets, but full truth of those claims depends on policies beyond screenshot evidence.

claims.claim: Recruiting pages communicate perks, benefits, or value propositions near job discovery content.
The stated perks and benefits are actual employment benefits under current policy.

items.evidence_note: Visible benefit messaging is present, but the truth or policy status of the benefit claims cannot be verified from screenshots.
items.rationale: The communication aspect is supported, while the real-world validity of the perks is hidden.

items.text: The system shall provide an alternative discovery path for corporate or non-park-specific careers.
items.annotation_notes: The careers pages include a distinct View Corporate Careers action, indicating that applicants are not limited to a single park-based path.

claims.claim: The careers page provides a distinct path for corporate or non-park-specific careers.
The alternative path is visually separate from the park-selection path.

items.evidence_note: The View Corporate Careers button is visible below the park selector.
items.rationale: The visible UI offers an alternative career discovery path outside a single park.

items.text: The system shall support narrowing opportunities within a selected park through structured categories or similar organization rather than only a flat undifferentiated job list.

claims.claim: The selected park page organizes opportunities through structured categories or team cards.
The visible organization is not only a flat undifferentiated job list.

items.evidence_note: Step 5 shows structured opportunity areas such as Food & Beverage, Lifeguards, Retail, Security, Admissions, and More Opportunities.
items.rationale: The park page visibly supports narrowing by structured opportunity areas.

items.text: The system shall surface recruiting campaigns or hiring events associated with a park's employment opportunities.

claims.claim: The selected park recruiting page surfaces a recruiting campaign or hiring event.
The hiring event is associated with the park employment page content.

items.evidence_note: Step 5 shows a Mega Hiring Event section within the Six Flags White Water recruiting page.
items.rationale: The visible park recruiting page includes event-style hiring campaign content.

items.text: The system shall present available parks in a browsable location list that helps applicants find the correct property.

claims.claim: Available parks are presented in a browsable location list.
The browsable location list helps applicants find the correct property.

items.evidence_note: Step 3 shows a browsable park list grouped by location. Step 4 shows a selected park after using that discovery mechanism.
items.rationale: The flow demonstrates list-based park discovery and selection.

items.text: The system shall make the recruiting flow understandable through consistent labeling of park, team, and role context across screens.

claims.claim: The recruiting flow uses consistent park-context labeling.
The recruiting flow uses consistent team-context labeling.
The recruiting flow uses consistent role-context labeling.

items.evidence_note: The flow repeatedly shows White Water park context, team cards, and a Lifeguard role detail page.
items.rationale: The observed labels keep park, team, and role context coherent across the recruiting path.

items.text: The system shall keep the selected park context attached when an applicant proceeds from recruiting content into the application-start flow for a specific opening.

claims.claim: The selected park context remains attached when an applicant proceeds from recruiting content to a specific opening.
The selected park context remains attached inside the application-start flow for the specific opening.

items.evidence_note: The flow preserves the park context through the job detail page, but it does not show the application-start flow after Apply now.
items.rationale: Context attachment is supported up to the chosen opening, while the application-start portion is not captured.

items.text: The system shall provide a visible handoff into the application process for the chosen role, such as a dedicated application page or explicit confirmation that the selected opening is being applied to.

claims.claim: The chosen role has an entry action into the application process.
The visible handoff provides a dedicated application page or explicit confirmation that the selected opening is being applied to.

items.evidence_note: Step 6 shows an Apply now action for the chosen role, but no downstream application page or confirmation is shown.
items.rationale: The application entry action is supported, but the handoff outcome is not visible.

items.text: The system shall let applicants drill into every visible department or team area on a selected park recruiting page to reach openings or recruiting details for that area.

claims.claim: Applicants can drill into at least one department or team area on a selected park recruiting page.
Applicants can drill into every visible department or team area on a selected park recruiting page.
Drilling into those areas reaches openings or recruiting details for that area.

items.evidence_note: The park recruiting page shows multiple team areas with Apply Now actions, and the flow reaches a Lifeguard opening. The flow does not test every visible team area.
items.rationale: The observed drill-in path is supported for one area, but the universal every-area requirement is not fully covered.

items.text: The system shall mark roles as featured or hiring only when those openings are still actively accepting applications.

claims.claim: Roles are marked as featured or hiring.
Roles are marked as featured or hiring only when those openings are still actively accepting applications.

items.evidence_note: The flow shows hiring labels and Apply Now actions, but it does not verify whether the openings are still actively accepting applications.
items.rationale: The core only-when correctness condition depends on non-visible job availability or application status.

items.text: The system shall provide a review step that summarizes the selected park and opening before the applicant commits to starting the application.

claims.claim: A review step summarizes the selected park and opening before the applicant commits to starting the application.
The applicant can commit to starting the application.

items.evidence_note: Steps 5 and 6 show direct Apply Now or Apply now actions with no intervening review summary visible before those actions.
items.rationale: The relevant pre-application screens visibly lack the required review summary.

items.text: The system shall provide direct in-page filtering or refinement within a selected park's opportunities, such as narrowing visible openings by department, job type, or similar criteria instead of relying only on static category entry points.

claims.claim: A selected park's opportunities provide direct in-page filtering or refinement.
Opportunities can be narrowed by department, job type, or similar criteria through direct in-page filtering or refinement.
Narrowing opportunities does not rely only on static category entry points.

items.evidence_note: Step 5 shows static team/category cards and Apply Now actions, but no filter input, refinement control, department filter, or job-type filter.
items.rationale: The shown park recruiting page visibly contradicts the stronger direct in-page filtering requirement.
